text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn confirms considering adjusting tax on very rich in the 1998 budget.
-- Boeing renounces three of its exclusive supply contracts with U.S. airlines. European Commission to decide today on whether to allow a planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.

-- LVMH increased stake in GrandMet to above 11 percent yesterday, sold shares in Guinness. Move is seen as part of bid by LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault to block a planned merger between GrandMet and Guinness.
-- Renault workers at Vilvoorde approve terms of layoff plan to accompany planned closure of the assembly plant.
-- Dutch insurers' association Eureko interested in bidding for GAN.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said to be preparing further austerity measures for 1998 budget, an additional 50 billion franc cut in public deficit seen necessary to meet the Maastricht treaty criteria.
-- French long-term rates move towards record lows.
-- Credit Agricole to sell stake in Union Financiere de France Banque (UFF) to Commercial Union for an estimated 1.3 billion francs.
-- Eridania Beghin Say buys 45 percent of leading oilseeds crushing company in Poland.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Hike in tax on corporate profits expected to hit some 25,000 businesses with a turnover above 50 million francs, having an impact on one out of two workers in the private sector.
-- Eyeware chain Alain Afflelou sells a 70 percent stake in his group to investment fund Alpha, whose main shareholder is CGIP.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Economist Jean-Paul Fitoussi is quoted as saying the government's plans to tax corporate profits will also hit households, as firms may resort to cost-cutting notably on wages, to balance a heavier tax burden.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- EU expected to approve planned merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas after Boeing made last-minute concessions dropping its status as exclusive supplier with three U.S. airlines.

-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn in an interview says "a great deal of restructuring in the public sector, in the labour market and in the welfare state has not taken place in France as much as it has in other countries", also says "I think unemployment will be flat at the same level for some time and will decrease from its current level at the end of 1998".
